thread:
incident-bot: P1 alert - us-west-2 serving pools experiencing tail amplification. p95/p99 up 4-6x, 5xx creeping ~0.9% in last 8m. paging on-call.
zoe_oncall: acknowledged, pulling runtime + infra. are customers reporting timeouts?
sara_cs: two customers opened urgent tickets; both saw streaming stop mid-response and some 504s. one on a support bridge now. no data integrity issues.
omar_runtime: looking at traces. traffic pattern: bursty small requests (avg tokens small) arriving in tight windows. continuous batching currently tuned aggressively for micro-latency so batches are too skinny and we have kernel-switch overhead. KV cache churn also visible. recommended live mitigation: widen batch window and make continuous batching more permissive to coalesce bursts.
felix_infra: autoscaler attempted to add nodes but hit reserved quota for our region; we should apply runtime mitigation instead of waiting on capacity. I can push control-plane configs.
zoe_oncall: list safe, immediate knobs we can flip now. please include expected customer UX impact.
omar_runtime: safe changes via control plane (ranked):
- set serving.batch.max_wait_ms 25 -> 300 (more time to aggregate requests; increases median latency for tiny requests)
- set serving.batch.continuous.merge_adjacent=true and continuous.max_delay_ms=220 (encourage joining of nearby batches)
- optionally raise serving.batch.min_batch_tokens from 32 -> 192 (forces denser batches; coordinate with infra for memory)
- temporarily disable streaming for redwood-base-3b in us-west-2 (cuts per-request bookkeeping, stops chunked responses)
- apply soft QPS shaping for top noisy API keys (avoid hard errors)
Impact: max_wait bump gives fastest reduction in tail spikes; disabling streaming affects UX but will not drop responses (clients get full response after completion). min_batch_tokens is higher risk due to memory.
felix_infra: I'll apply (1) + merge_adjacent now, watch for regressions, then we can apply key-shaping if needed. commands: ```
redwoodctl config set serving.batch.max_wait_ms=300 --scope=us-west-2 --apply-live
redwoodctl config set serving.batch.continuous.merge_adjacent=true --scope=us-west-2 --apply-live
redwoodctl config set serving.batch.continuous.max_delay_ms=220 --scope=us-west-2 --apply-live
```
deploy-bot: config-change: serving.batch.max_wait_ms updated (user=felix_infra) -> rollout id 9851, targeting pools usw2-1..5
omar_runtime: tail logs show rapid improvement ~30s after change. excerpt: ```
23:01:42 queue_depth=154 p99=2800ms
23:02:10 queue_depth=38 p99=640ms
23:02:38 queue_depth=12 p99=340ms
```
sara_cs: customers on bridge confirm fewer timeouts, but one reports their streaming consumer saw a longer wait before final response. explained tradeoff and they're okay for now.
mike_product: note: disabling streaming will break real-time previews for some customers. please record which customers rely on streaming and notify product owners if we keep it off >20m.
zoe_oncall: if tail still > threshold in 3-4m, next step is disable streaming for model redwood-base-3b in region and apply per-key shaping for top noisy keys. Felix, can you prepare quota commands?
felix_infra: prepping targeted shaping for keys now. sample commands: ```
redwoodctl quota update --api-key key-ENTERPRISE1 --qps 6 --scope=us-west-2 --reason "live-shape-noisy-key"
redwoodctl quota update --api-key key-SANDBOX --qps 10 --scope=us-west-2 --reason "mitigation"
```
deploy-bot: quota-change accepted (user=felix_infra) -> change id 9872, effective immediately
omar_runtime: enabling streaming=false for redwood-base-3b in us-west-2 to cut per-request overhead. command: ```
redwoodctl config set serving.streaming.enabled=false --model=redwood-base-3b --scope=us-west-2 --apply-live
```
deploy-bot: config-change: serving.streaming.enabled=false updated (user=omar_runtime) -> rollout id 9856
omar_runtime: after shaping + streaming off, metrics stabilized. p99 down to ~380-450ms, p95 ~270ms, 5xx ~0.09%. logs: ```
23:04:05 queue_depth=66 p99=980ms 5xx=0.19%
23:04:40 queue_depth=18 p99=420ms 5xx=0.08%
23:05:12 queue_depth=7 p99=360ms 5xx=0.05%
```
sara_cs: support bridge reports improved behavior. one customer still wants a rollback ETA; told them we'll validate in canary then stage rollback.
mike_product: please create a short customer-facing note if streaming remains disabled beyond 15m. also list SDKs that depend on chunked streams.
\eomar_runtime: (private note) increasing max_wait_ms improves throughput by allowing larger batches to form; expect median increase ~80-160ms for sub-200-token requests. we'll run a canary at 120ms later tonight and consider ramping down from 300ms to a smaller value once traffic calms.
felix_infra: autoscaler ticket for reserved quota submitted; estimated action in 30-50m. mitigations bought us time.
zoe_oncall: updating PD incident: applied mitigations (batch.max_wait_ms=300, continuous.merge_adjacent=true, continuous.max_delay_ms=220, streaming disabled for redwood-base-3b in us-west-2, targeted per-key QPS shaping). Customer impact: fewer timeouts and errors, degraded streaming UX, slightly higher median for tiny requests.
sara_cs: customers notified; one asked to be alerted when streaming resumes. logged.
zoe_oncall: handoff: Omar monitor for next 50m; I'll hand to night oncall at 00:00 UTC. Escalate if p99 > 700ms or 5xx > 0.5%. Document exact commands + rollback steps in incident playbook.
omar_runtime: ack. adjusted paging thresholds: p95>600ms pages. will post updates every 10m.
zoe_oncall: thanks team. incident-bot: mark P1 -> mitigated and keep channel open for verification. good work.
incident-bot: Incident P1 status changed -> mitigated. channel will remain open for 60m.
